origins.section: A Zone Written as an Offset Has No Rules
Near a Clock Change a Local Time Can Be Missing or Doubled, and ZonedDateTime Picks One Without Telling You
withZoneSameInstant Converts a Moment; withZoneSameLocal Moves It
Store a Future Appointment as Local Time and Zone, and Work Out the Instant Late

gates.says: all 4 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-parsed-offset-rehearsal: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-parsed-offset-rehearsal: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-parsed-offset-rehearsal: c is decided by working from the page. Lines 58-59 say text without a region name parses to a ZoneOffset zone whose rules are '+01:00 forever', so it 'behaves like the OffsetDateTime above', and output line 54 shows plusWeeks keeping +01:00. Lines 35-36 say the OffsetDateTime 'kept +01:00: its 09:00 is 08:00 UTC, which an Amsterdam phone shows as 10:00', and output lines 30-31 show it. Applied to this stem: 19:00+02:00 is 17:00 UTC, which is 18:00 in Berlin at +01:00.
recorded.prompt:q-meter-reading-overlap: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-meter-reading-overlap: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-meter-reading-overlap: a is decided by line 109: 'In an overlap `of` takes the earlier offset'. Output line 104 shows ZonedDateTime.of at 2026-10-25T02:30 resolving to +02:00, the offset in force before the change, and line 99 with output line 105 shows withLaterOffsetAtOverlap() picking the second occurrence. The example is Amsterdam; the stem supplies Denver's dates and offsets.
recorded.prompt:q-webinar-same-local: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-webinar-same-local: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-webinar-same-local: b is decided by lines 83-84: 'withZoneSameLocal keeps the wall clock, which names a moment five hours later: a colleague shown that invite joins after the call has ended'. Output line 77 shows the local time kept (15:00-04:00). Applied to this stem: 16:00 at -05:00 is 21:00 UTC, five hours after 16:00 UTC.
recorded.prompt:q-dentist-saved-instant: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-dentist-saved-instant: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-dentist-saved-instant: b is decided by working from lines 157-178. Line 157 says that 'Saving it as an Instant fixes today's offset'. Output line 171 shows the saved instant kept unchanged and read with the new offset, giving a different wall time, and line 175 says it 'now reads 08:00'. In the page's example the offset falls by an hour, so the time moves earlier. Here it rises, from -03:00 to -02:00: 17:00 UTC read at -02:00 is 15:00.

recorded.prompt:q-parsed-offset-rehearsal:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-parsed-offset-rehearsal:a: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-parsed-offset-rehearsal:a: Refuted by lines 58-60: the zone is a ZoneOffset, 'as ZoneId.of("+01:00") would give', and 'Nor can an offset name the region'. Output line 54 shows the zone printed as +01:00. The Reference row for ZoneId.of("+01:00") reads 'a ZoneOffset: one fixed offset'.
recorded.prompt:q-parsed-offset-rehearsal:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-parsed-offset-rehearsal:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-parsed-offset-rehearsal:b: Refuted by the analogue in lines 35-36: a value that keeps the old offset is a different reading on the region's clocks ('which an Amsterdam phone shows as 10:00'), and output line 31 shows this. Partly true: the reason given (the zone is a fixed +02:00 that plusWeeks keeps) is correct, and the value itself prints as 19:00+02:00. It is wrong only because the stem asks for the time on Berlin's clocks.
recorded.prompt:q-parsed-offset-rehearsal:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-parsed-offset-rehearsal:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-parsed-offset-rehearsal:d: Its premise is refuted by lines 58-60: no region and no rules are looked up. Output line 29 shows a region-zoned value keeping 09:00 on the wall clock across the change.
